subject: Post-demo: deployment economics & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@praxis-analytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: deployment economics & next steps

Jordan — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our call: 

- Current priority: stable low-latency inference for customer-facing features (feedback from PM: 100–250ms p95).
- Data sensitivity: production telemetry and PII in inputs — SOC 2 + VPC/network isolation important.
- Expected steady-state load: ~150 reqs/sec (avg), peaks up to ~600 reqs/sec for short bursts.
- Monthly token estimate (current prompts + responses): ~120M input tokens / 360M output tokens (~480M tokens/month).

From a deployment standpoint you flagged three options we should model: Hosted (pay-as-you-go), Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC or on-prem). To make the comparison actionable I propose we produce three scenarios with unit economics and performance expectations:

1) Hosted API: per-token pricing, no infra commitment, fastest time to launch, built-in multi-tenant security controls.
2) Dedicated: reserved GPU pool with a monthly commit (we'll show 3 commit tiers); lower $/token at scale, predictable throughput, optional burst capacity.
3) Private VPC / on-prem: fixed monthly platform fee + infra OPEX (we'll estimate OPEX and one-time onboarding).

Ask from you: can you confirm the 480M token/month ballpark and whether the 100–250ms p95 target is a hard SLO or a guideline? That will change the commit sizing. Also please share the procurement timeline (I saw there was a doc attached in the folder — please re-send if that changed).

Next steps (I’ll coordinate this side):
- I’ll send a concise pricing comparison (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) with an expected cost range and recommended commit tiers by EOD tomorrow.
- Rishi will produce committed-capacity sizing (GPU count + slots) for Dedicated and Private.
- Vivek will draft the latency/availability SLOs and fallback policy language for the procurement team.

I attached a short high-level pricing summary to get the ball rolling.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142
redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood_high_level_pricing.pdf
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@praxis-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment economics & next steps

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Confirming a few things from our side: 

- Token estimate: the 480M/month is accurate based on our current prompts; we'll re-run with the new prompt templates next week and flag any changes.
- Latency SLO: 100–250ms p95 is what Product is asking for on the user-facing path. If we can’t hit 250ms consistently we’ll need to route to a simpler model or cache.
- Compliance: SOC 2 is required for our procurement; full VPC isolation is strongly preferred for the PI roadmap but not mandatory on day one.

Procurement timeline: we need pricing and legal redlines for our vendor shortlist by 2026-04-02. I attached our internal timeline for visibility. Procurement will likely ask for 6–12 month committed pricing vs pay-as-you-go.

Can you include: a side-by-side monthly cost estimate for the three deployment modes, the break-even commit level (months/tokens) where Dedicated becomes cheaper than Hosted, and a short note on how caching/batching affects unit economics?

Jordan
Head of Platform Product, Praxis Analytics
Jordan.Hayes@praxis-analytics.com
Attachment: praxis_procurement_timeline.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-20T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: deployment economics & next steps

Rishi / Vivek — forwarding Jordan's confirmation and procurement timeline. Can you split the work as follows and target an internal draft by EOD tomorrow so I can share with Praxis?

Rishi: please build three cost scenarios for the 480M token/month baseline (Hosted PAYG, Dedicated - 3 commit tiers e.g. 2, 4, 8 GPUs, Private VPC estimate including 1x infra AMI + support). For Dedicated include: monthly price, $/token effective at expected utilization (assume 70% steady utilization + 30% bursts), and the break-even month count where committed pricing undercuts Hosted PAYG. Add a short note about optional quantization/throughput knobs that could reduce GPU needs.

Vivek: draft a short SLO pack (latency p50/p95 targets, availability, failover policy to a smaller model or Hosted fallback) and an operations note on KV cache retention and data residency constraints (SOC 2 + customer-managed KMS). If we can, include a quick list of fallback policies that preserve user experience but reduce cost.

I’ll stitch both into a single doc and send to Jordan + procurement.

Thanks — Marissa

On Fri, Mar 20, 2026 at 09:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jordan — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our call:

Date: 2026-03-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment economics & next steps

Marissa — that plan works. Procurement wants the numbers in a short deck (one slide per deployment mode) + a single line item redline on the Master Services Agreement. Can you confirm you can deliver: 

- One-slide cost comparison (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with expected monthly cost ranges and the break-even month for a 12-month commit.
- An operations SLO summary (1 page) we can attach to the SOW.
- A point of contact for legal to send a first-pass MSA (Procurement will expect to see standard security appendices).

Timeline: if we can get the one-slide + SLO summary by close of business 2026-03-22, procurement will put Redwood on the shortlist for the April review. Who should I expect on the call when we do the pricing walkthrough?

Jordan
